boundary: Primary demo packaging for the deterministic browser-local maintained app shell only; no new simulation organ, no LLM call, no subjective consciousness, no real consent, no autonomous natural language, no moral patienthood, no production persistence, no finished gameplay, no complete 3D engine, and no metaphysical frequency claim.

manual_playtest_steps.action: Start a local server from the repo root with python3 -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1.
manual_playtest_steps.expected_evidence: Primary demo launcher opens at the localhost URL.
manual_playtest_steps.proves: reviewers have one stable URL-style entrypoint instead of hunting report artifacts

manual_playtest_steps.action: Open the primary demo launcher and read the boundary before launching.
manual_playtest_steps.expected_evidence: Boundary says deterministic browser-local shell and no consciousness/LLM/product claim.
manual_playtest_steps.proves: the no-overclaim boundary is visible before play

manual_playtest_steps.action: Launch a clean session using the Clean demo button.
manual_playtest_steps.expected_evidence: The maintained v61 shell opens with ?reset=1 and a primary-demo source tag.
manual_playtest_steps.proves: the launcher targets the single maintained shell, not a forked simulation

manual_playtest_steps.action: Enter the world and move at least twice.
manual_playtest_steps.expected_evidence: Room/status fields update and replay rows increase.
manual_playtest_steps.proves: arrival and movement remain usable through the primary path

manual_playtest_steps.action: Talk through the bounded phrase control, then ask schedule.
manual_playtest_steps.expected_evidence: Resident memory/schedule fields update without open-ended chat claims.
manual_playtest_steps.proves: bounded conversation and resident schedule inspection are still on the same surface

manual_playtest_steps.action: Borrow and return the awning tool.
manual_playtest_steps.expected_evidence: Debt increases, then returns to zero while trust repairs partially.
manual_playtest_steps.proves: visible consequence and non-magical trust repair are observable

manual_playtest_steps.action: Wait offscreen, then inspect schedule/progress again.
manual_playtest_steps.expected_evidence: Progress changes while the avatar is idle/absent.
manual_playtest_steps.proves: offscreen life is visible in the primary shell

manual_playtest_steps.expected_evidence: Saved avatar/resident values return after restore.
manual_playtest_steps.proves: local persistence and rollback are part of the playable loop

manual_playtest_steps.expected_evidence: Checklist reports 10 checks and all pass.
manual_playtest_steps.proves: the internal QA hooks still cover the maintained tasks

manual_playtest_steps.action: Run state-boundary and save/restore smoke hooks.
manual_playtest_steps.expected_evidence: Both hook rows pass and no private workspace/LLM keys appear in public trace.
A prepared replay export link appears and export bytes are nonzero.
manual_playtest_steps.proves: review/debug evidence can be captured without relying on blocked downloads

manual_playtest_steps.action: Close the shell, reopen the primary launcher, then use Resume demo.
manual_playtest_steps.expected_evidence: The resumed shell keeps persisted world state unless Clean demo is used.
manual_playtest_steps.proves: leave/return continuity is part of the manual review path

next_gate: post-303: use the stable primary demo entrypoint for all browser-world work, run the manual playtest script against real defects, and harden the same shell before adding any new world-system report
scope_guards: Only the primary demo launcher is new; gameplay still lives in the maintained v61 app shell.
The manual script uses Report 302 browser evidence as the baseline, not as a substitute for future human playtests.
The launcher gives clean and resume paths so persistence bugs can be reproduced rather than hidden.
The boundary remains visible before launch and inside the shell.
Future browser-world work should patch this shell unless a defect proves a new surface is necessary.
